Think of your brain like a big city with lots of roads. For a long time, scientists knew that certain areas helped with decisions, like whether to act on an impulse or hold back, but they couldn’t see how the roads actually connected. Now, using new imaging tools, researchers have started to map those connections in detail, and they’ve found a small hub that acts like a gatekeeper. It decides which signals get through and which get stopped. When it works well, you can resist that second slice of cake; when it doesn’t, impulses win more often. The map might help explain conditions like addiction and ADHD, and someday it could point to better treatments.
